triples.relationship: Wisdom parallel: guarded silence in the presence of evil
triples.rationale: Amos says the understanding person will be silent because the time is evil, following the description of hostility to reproof and corrupt judgment. The psalmist guards his mouth when the sinner stands against him, becoming mute and silent even from good things. Both connect restrained speech to a hostile moral setting. The psalm gives a personal concern about sinning with the tongue and continuing pain, rather than a rule that all speech in every evil time is forbidden.
triples.source_text: Therefore the understanding person will be silent at that time, because it is an evil time.

target_units.text: I said, “I will guard my ways so as not to sin with my tongue.” I placed a guard upon my mouth when the sinner stood against me.
I became mute and was humbled and kept silent from good things, and my pain was renewed.

triples.relationship: Personification: building elements give voice amid judgment
triples.rationale: Amos makes the temple's coffered ceilings wail in a scene of many fallen and imposed silence. Habakkuk says a stone cries from a wall, while condemning a house's shame and a city built through bloodshed. Both give voice to part of a building within an oracle against destructive wrongdoing. The temple ceilings are not identified with Habakkuk's wall, and the target's beetle from wood is preserved rather than rewritten as a speaking timber beam.
triples.source_text: The temple’s coffered ceilings will wail. On that day,” says the Lord, “many have fallen in every place. I will cast silence upon them.”

target_units.text: You planned shame for your house, brought many peoples to an end, and your soul sinned.
For a stone will cry from a wall, and a beetle from wood will utter these things.
Woe to the one building a city with bloodshed and preparing a city with injustices!
